Triggers.value: A specific texture associated with the event
The same time of day the event occurred

Threat.value: I find it harder to feel safe at night than during the day
Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building

Memory.value: The memory feels like it belongs to someone else rather than to me
Remembering the event brings back the same terror I felt at the time
Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning

Negative Appraisals.value: There is something wrong with me as a person
I used to be a happy person but now I am always miserable.
The world is a dangerous place

issues.item: Triggers: Visual (Needles/Medical): Medical equipment such as needles or drips
issues.explanation: A medical-equipment visual trigger is hard to reconcile as a central combat-related trigger for this profile, especially alongside otherwise combat-consistent threat items and without any medical/hospital-related memory or appraisal content. It suggests a different trauma context and is clinically difficult to integrate with the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Memory: Rage on Recall + Emotionless Recall + Memory Feels Alien
issues.explanation: Within Memory, intense rage on recall conflicts with the paired reports of emotionally numb recall and the memory feeling alien/detached. Fluctuation can occur, but as a compact three-item profile these items pull in opposing directions—high emotional arousal versus marked dissociative detachment—without other memory content to bridge them.

Memory: Rage on Recall + Emotionless Recall + Memory Feels Alien

issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, 'Rage on Recall' conflicts with the paired endorsement of markedly detached recall ('Emotionless Recall' and 'Memory Feels Alien'). Intense rage during recall and recall experienced as numb/alien can both occur in PTSD, but selecting all three as coequal memory descriptors creates a direct within-node tension between highly affect-laden remembering and strongly depersonalized, affectless remembering. The rest of the profile coherently reflects severe combat-related PTSD, but this specific Memory combination is the main clinically questionable inconsistency.

issues.item: Emotionless Recall: Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger
issues.explanation: Within the Memory node, two items describe markedly detached/derealized recall ('emotionless', 'belongs to someone else') while another describes intensely affect-laden reliving ('same terror I felt at the time'). These can both occur across different moments in PTSD, but as the only three selected memory items they pull in opposing directions and are not a clean, internally coherent depiction of a single dominant memory style for this profile.

These two appraisals are plausible in severe PTSD, but for a 63-year-old married airline pilot they create a hard-to-explain mismatch with the rest of the profile when presented without any trauma-linked appraisal content. 'I have no future' is especially discordant for an older, still-employed patient and is not well integrated with the combat-specific trigger/threat pattern. The Negative Appraisals node is dominated by global depressive identity/future statements rather than trauma-related meanings that would plausibly connect to the very strong Triggers → Negative Appraisals edge in the formulation.

vignette: Kai'a, a 63-year-old Oceania man and seasoned airline pilot, sat in his favorite armchair, staring out the window at the night sky. As an experienced flier, he had grown accustomed to the hum of engines and the whir of propellers, but tonight, every creak of the house made him twitch. It was as if his body had become attuned to a different frequency – one that resonated with the memories he tried to keep at bay. Twenty years ago, Kai'a was a young soldier, deployed in a war-torn country. On a fateful evening, around dusk, his unit came under attack near an abandoned airfield. The sounds of gunfire and explosions still echoed in his mind, but it was the feel of rough canvas against his skin that transported him back to that chaotic moment. A specific texture associated with the makeshift medical tent where he'd been treated for shrapnel wounds now haunted him. As night descended, Kai'a's vigilance increased. He found himself checking the locks on every door and window, a habit his wife had grown accustomed to but couldn't understand. She would try to reassure him that they were safe in their suburban home, but Kai'a knew better – the world was a treacherous place. His gaze darted toward potential exits whenever he entered a new space, mentally mapping escape routes as if preparing for an emergency landing. On occasion, when least expected, the roar of a helicopter or aircraft would shatter his composure. The sounds transported him to that fateful day, and memories flooded back like a tidal wave. His body tensed, bracing itself for impact. Remembering was not just recollection; it was reliving – every scream, every scent, every snap of gunfire. Terror washed over him anew with each recall. Kai'a struggled to reconcile the man he used to be with who he'd become. Before the war, flying brought him joy; now it filled him with dread. He couldn't shake the feeling that something fundamental was wrong within him – as if his psyche had been irrevocably damaged by what he'd witnessed and endured. As a pilot, Kai'a's days were structured around strict protocols, precision, and order. Yet, despite this veneer of control, his nights now swirled with anxiety and fear. His wife sensed the darkness gathering within him but didn't know how to intervene. Kai'a felt lost in this new reality – forever bound to a narrative he'd rather forget. When discussing the past with his family or therapist, Kai'a found himself detached from his own experiences, as if describing events from someone else's life story. It was an odd disconnection that unnerved him further. He sensed an abyss between who he thought he was and this stranger living in his skin. Over time, avoidance behaviors crept into his routine. Avoiding social gatherings or noisy areas where aircraft sounds might trigger memories became increasingly common. His friends noticed the change but didn't push; they assumed it was just a phase born from weariness after decades of flying. Kai'a's loved ones sensed that something was amiss, but their gentle prodding only intensified his self-doubt. As he struggled to navigate this labyrinthine world within him, Kai'a finally acknowledged the exhaustion that accompanied living in a state of perpetual vigilance. A recent incident on a flight – where an unexpected helicopter flew low overhead, shattering his composure mid-air – had pushed him toward seeking help. With each ticking night, as sounds from the outside world blended with those echoes from his past, Kai'a realized he couldn't outrun these demons forever. Perhaps it was time to confront them head-on and break free from this perpetual state of high alert.
